newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget talks to resume next Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget talks to resume next Wednesday.

text.p: White House and congressional budget negotiatiors said on Thursday they will resume talks on Wednesday next week. A key participant, Senate Budget chief Pete Domenici, said he has no plans to pursue agreement on a budget outside of the formal talks.

Republicans had said earlier that if agreement were not reached by the end of this week they would seek to work out a separate deal with conservative Democrats. White House budget chief Frank Raines said there was no deadline for completion of a deal. "I think everybody acknowledges we are making progress and we hope we can bring it to conclusion," he said.
"There is absolutely no guarantee that we can bring it to a successful conclusion," Raines added. "There are no time limits," he said at the conclusion of the talks for the week.
Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said the negotiators had examined the federal budget thoroughly and would return to some of the thornier issues such as tax cuts, Medicare and Medicaid, next week.

"I am not proceeding on any other front," he said when asked about comments of Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, Republican of Mississippi, that negotiations with a group of conservative Democrats would begin if no budget deal were reached this week.
"I prefer to see if we can get the president on board and I think he wants to be on board... We want to give it a few more days," Domenici added.

"We may shock you in the next five or six days," he told reporters at the conclusion of talks on the international affairs budget. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin participated for the White House. In addition to Domenici, House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, Republican of Ohio, and the two senior Democrats on the budget committees, Sen Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey and John Spratt of South Carolina participated.
